skill.description: Apple Human Interface Guidelines reference for widgets, Live Activities, notifications, complications, quick actions, Top Shelf, App Clips, and App Shortcuts.
skill.summary: Design Apple system experience components using focused HIG guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Apple HIG documentation terms, Markdown image text, inline code formatting, and attribution links. I found no evidence of prompt injection, executable commands, active network behavior, malware intent, or data exfiltration in the reviewed skill files.

content.value_statement: Apple system surfaces have strict layout, privacy, and interaction constraints. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused HIG guidance for choosing and shaping those surfaces.
actual_capabilities: Recommends the best Apple system surface for a product use case.
Summarizes design rules for widgets, complications, and Live Activities.
Guides notification content, actions, privacy, and watchOS presentation.
Explains App Clips, App Shortcuts, Home Screen quick actions, and Top Shelf patterns.
Structures advice around content strategy, update frequency, variants, and deep links.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not production Swift or SwiftUI implementation.
It does not validate current App Store Review requirements.
It cannot replace testing on real devices and platform versions.
It depends on the included local references staying current with Apple guidance.

use_cases.title: Choose A System Surface
use_cases.description: Compare widgets, Live Activities, notifications, App Clips, and App Shortcuts for one product scenario.

use_cases.title: Review Component Concepts
use_cases.description: Check proposed layouts for privacy, glanceability, update cadence, and platform-specific constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Platform Experiences
use_cases.description: Map one app feature across iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Mac, CarPlay, and visionOS surfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Pick A Component
prompt_templates.prompt: I am designing [feature] for [platform]. Recommend the best Apple system experience component and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Improve A Widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this widget concept for Apple HIG fit: [concept]. Cover content, size variants, interactivity, privacy, and deep links.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Live Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a system experience plan for [time-bound event]. Include Live Activities, notifications, update frequency, end state, and fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Surface Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Apple system surfaces for [app]: [surfaces]. Identify conflicts, redundant content, privacy risks, and platform-specific changes.

output_examples.input: A food delivery app wants status visible outside the main app.
output_examples.output: Recommend a Live Activity for active orders, notification alerts only for essential changes, and deep links to order details.

output_examples.input: A finance app wants a Home Screen widget with portfolio value.
output_examples.output: Show high-level trends, avoid sensitive account details, support useful sizes, and open the relevant portfolio screen on tap.

output_examples.input: A streaming app wants tvOS Top Shelf content.
output_examples.output: Feature new or personalized content, avoid ads and prices, provide dynamic previews, and include a static fallback image.

best_practices: Start with the user need, then choose the smallest system surface that satisfies it.
Keep visible content glanceable, private, and directly related to the current task.
Define update cadence, variants, and deep links before polishing visual details.
anti_patterns: Do not use Live Activities, widgets, or Top Shelf as advertising space.
Do not duplicate a full app screen inside a small system surface.
Do not expose personal or confidential information on public device surfaces.

faq.question: Does this skill write SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Apple HIG design guidance and planning, not implementation code.

faq.question: Which Apple surfaces does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers widgets, Live Activities, notifications, complications, quick actions, Top Shelf, App Clips, and App Shortcuts.

faq.question: Can it help choose between widgets and Live Activities?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares static glanceable content with time-bound, frequently updated experiences.

faq.question: Does it include privacy guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights when content may be visible on Lock Screen, watch face, or shared device contexts.

faq.question: Is it useful for product reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure critiques around content, interaction, update frequency, variants, and deep-link behavior.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes included references and should be checked against current Apple documentation for release decisions.
